name: Ningyuan Xu
description: Ningyuan Xu — M.Sc. student at Nanyang Technological University, working on surface science, wetting and depletion-driven colloidal assembly.
intro: I study how surface structure, chemistry and particle interactions influence wetting and colloidal organisation. My work connects experimental surface engineering with computational approaches to soft matter.
about: I am an M.Sc. student in Chemical Modelling at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore, supervised by Assoc. Prof. Ran Ni. My current research focuses on Monte Carlo modelling of depletion-driven colloidal assembly, including how deviations in particle shape influence chiral selection and self-sorting.

Previously, I worked as an undergraduate research assistant at the Center for Materials Surface Science, UESTC, under Professors Dehui Wang and Xu Deng. There, I investigated durable superhydrophobic coatings and droplet–surface interactions. I hold B.Eng. degrees from UESTC and the University of Glasgow.

research.title: From particle shape to colloidal assembly
research.description: Investigating how particle geometry and depletion interactions influence collective ordering, chiral selection and self-sorting.
research.alt: Conceptual line drawing of differently oriented polyhedral colloids and smaller depletant particles.
research.details: I am developing a modular C++ Monte Carlo framework for hard particles and implicit ideal depletants. The work combines accelerated overlap detection, checkpoint/restart and literature benchmarks, and compares pairwise and many-body descriptions of depletion.

research.title: Durable surfaces for water shedding
research.description: Designing sprayable, waterborne superhydrophobic coatings that combine hierarchical texture with practical durability.
research.alt: Conceptual drawing of a water droplet resting above a textured surface containing hollow microspheres.
research.details: My work at UESTC included formulation screening, silica surface functionalisation, spray deposition, dynamic wetting measurements, abrasion and environmental ageing tests. One project uses silica nanoparticles and hollow glass microspheres to combine water shedding with a low-loss coating architecture for radomes.

research.title: Watching droplets meet structured materials
research.description: Using high-speed imaging and wetting measurements to understand droplet impact, penetration and liquid transport.
research.alt: Conceptual sequence of a droplet approaching a porous mesh, with three illustrative droplet shapes.
research.details: I assisted droplet-impact testing and 10,000-fps video production for a superhydrophilic–Janus bilayer window screen, and co-analysed penetration data. This work was published in Small in 2025.
